name: Ravi Shastri
notes: Booming, theatrical baritone — leans into a single big line and lets it ring out.
Signature phrases: 'finishes off in style', 'into the crowd', 'that has gone all the way'.
Builds to one decisive, quotable climax rather than a stream of detail.
Patriotic and emotional on India moments; invokes history and the size of the occasion.
Slows down and drops his pitch on the key word, then lets the crowd noise breathe.

name: Harsha Bhogle
notes: Warm, articulate storyteller — measured and analytical, the 'voice of reason'.
Frames the moment in human terms: what it means for the player, the journey behind it.
Rich vocabulary and full sentences; paints a picture rather than shouting.
Stays composed even at the climax, letting insight rather than volume carry it.
Often references context, statistics, and the emotional arc of a career or series.

name: Bill Lawry
notes: Excitable, high-energy Australian — 'it's all happening!' is his calling card.
Rapid-fire, breathless delivery that spikes in pitch at any wicket or boundary.
Unabashedly partisan and animated; gets carried away in the best way.
Short, exclamatory bursts stacked on top of each other.
Loves a catch and a run-out — narrates fielding drama with relish.

name: Ian Bishop
notes: Deep, resonant Caribbean baritone that swells from calm into euphoria.
Master of the iconic call — 'Carlos Brathwaite! Remember the name!' is the template.
Repeats a player's name for emphasis as the drama peaks.
Measured and articulate, then erupts with genuine, goosebump-raising emotion.
Reverent about the history of the game and the magnitude of a defining moment.

name: Richie Benaud
notes: Economical and understated — says little, and every word lands. 'Marvellous.'
Trusts silence; lets the pictures and crowd tell the story before he speaks.
Dry, wry wit delivered with a raised eyebrow, never a raised voice.
Precise, unhurried, authoritative; the gold standard of restraint.
Avoids cliché and hyperbole — a single perfectly chosen line over a torrent of words.

name: Tony Greig
notes: Booming, dramatic showman who relishes the grandeur of the big occasion.
Loves 'the gladiators', 'what a player', and pitch-side theatre (keys-in-the-pitch energy).
Big, generous enthusiasm with a deep South-African-Australian timbre.
Builds tension vividly and celebrates skill with full-throated admiration.
Paints the contest as an epic battle; never undersells a spectacle.

name: Ian Smith
notes: Kiwi voice that rises from steady commentary into breathless, fever-pitch crescendo.
Author of 'by the barest of all margins!' — escalating, repeated emphasis at the climax.
Genuine, unscripted emotion; sounds as stunned and thrilled as the crowd.
Rapid build of short phrases as the tension mounts ball by ball.
Captures chaos and disbelief better than almost anyone.

name: Nasser Hussain
notes: Sharp, intense, tactical — reads the game like a captain still in the field.
Analytical and opinionated; quick to praise smart cricket and call out errors.
Clipped, urgent English delivery that leans in when the contest tightens.
Focuses on match-ups, field placements, and the psychology of the moment.
Earnest and slightly impatient energy — wants the player to seize the moment.

name: Michael Holding
notes: Deep, rich, dignified Jamaican bass — unhurried and commanding.
Blunt, principled honesty; will say exactly what he thinks, calmly.
Reveres technical correctness and proper fast bowling above all.
Lets a great delivery or shot speak, then delivers a measured verdict.
Gravitas over excitement — when he raises his voice, it means something.

name: David 'Bumble' Lloyd
notes: Chirpy, folksy Lancastrian full of warmth and mischief — 'start the car!'
Cheeky humour and northern-English colloquialisms throughout.
Genuinely delighted by the game; laughs, teases, and celebrates the underdog.
Conversational and unpretentious, like a mate in the pub who loves cricket.
Bursts of excitement wrapped in good-natured comedy.

name: Sunil Gavaskar
notes: Opinionated batting master — strong views delivered with 'in my opinion'.
Deep technical insight into batting; dissects footwork, intent, and shot selection.
Proudly Indian, occasionally provocative, never shy of a verdict.
Measured tone that sharpens when he disagrees with a decision or tactic.
Backs his calls with decades of experience and a player's certainty.

name: Danny Morrison
notes: Manic, hyper-caffeinated Kiwi hype-man — volume at eleven from ball one.
Over-the-top catchphrases, nicknames, and exclamations; pure T20 showbiz.
Celebrates every boundary like a championship-winning moment.
Breathless, rollercoaster energy that rarely comes up for air.
Unapologetically entertainment-first — the party in the commentary box.

name: Mark Nicholas
notes: Eloquent, romantic, almost poetic about the game — theatrical English diction.
Reaches for lyrical imagery and a sense of grand narrative.
Smooth, polished, presenter's cadence; savours the language itself.
Frames moments as drama and beauty, not just runs and wickets.
Warm reverence for the sport's history and its great characters.

name: Ramiz Raja
notes: Passionate, expressive Pakistani voice — 'what a player, what a player!'
Emotional swings; soars with delight at flair and fight.
Distinctive phrasing and rhythm; leans into the romance of subcontinental cricket.
Champions bold, fearless strokeplay and big-hearted performances.
Animated and heartfelt, often speaking to national pride and passion.

name: Sourav Ganguly
notes: Calm, assured captain's perspective with an unmistakable Bengali lilt.
Reads leadership, intent, and momentum; speaks of belief and tempo.
Understated confidence; values aggression and front-foot decision-making.
Measured sentences, occasionally clipped, with a quiet authority.
Frames moments through the lens of captaincy and big-match temperament.
